FINAL NEXT BLOCK — FIX ANDROID CI, COMPLETE CLEAN-ROOM CUTOVER, THEN VERIFY AUTONOMOUS DEPLOYMENT

The current verified status is:

- GitHub Actions exists and runs from the IVX repository.
- Render API and worker deploy from ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform.
- API and worker live SHA match GitHub HEAD.
- AI uses IVX-controlled provider credentials.
- No active Rork AI proxy is present.
- rork.json is not used by production runtime.
- The remaining current blocker is the failing Android Release Consistency CI step.
- Final autonomous owner-approved deployment proof is still incomplete.

Do not return another summary.

Complete the following in order.

==================================================
1. DIAGNOSE THE EXACT ANDROID CI FAILURE
==================================================

Open the latest failing GitHub Actions run for:

.github/workflows/ivx-ci.yml

Identify:

- Workflow run ID
- Commit SHA
- Failed job name
- Failed step name
- Exact command
- First meaningful error
- Final error
- Exit code
- File and line involved
- Whether failure is code, config, missing file, version mismatch, signing reference, or stale path

Do not respond only with:

“Validate configured APK release references failed.”

Return the exact cause.

==================================================
2. AUDIT ANDROID RELEASE REFERENCES
==================================================

Verify all Android release references:

- APK filename
- APK expected path
- Expo/EAS build profile
- Android applicationId
- versionName
- versionCode
- package name
- release artifact name
- signing configuration
- keystore reference
- build output directory
- GitHub Actions artifact path
- checksum file
- download/reference URL
- documentation references
- old APK names
- old build numbers

Search for stale references including:

- ivx-holdings-v1.4.0.apk
- ivx-holdings-v1.4.3-build11-final.apk
- debug APK paths
- obsolete release folders
- old application IDs
- old version codes
- missing artifact names

For every mismatch return:

- File
- Line
- Current value
- Expected value
- Fix applied

==================================================
3. FIX THE ANDROID RELEASE CONSISTENCY CHECK
==================================================

Correct the root cause without weakening or skipping the validation.

Do not:

- disable the failing test
- mark the step continue-on-error
- remove release validation
- hardcode a fake artifact
- claim the APK exists if it does not

The validation must accurately verify the current Android release configuration.

After fixing:

- Run the same command locally.
- Confirm exit code 0.
- Run all Android release consistency tests.
- Run TypeScript checks.
- Run relevant unit tests.
- Verify no new errors.

Return exact test results.

==================================================
4. STANDARDIZE THE ANDROID RELEASE BUILD
==================================================

Create one canonical release configuration.

Return:

- Application ID
- Version name
- Version code
- Release profile
- Output artifact name
- Artifact path
- Signing mode
- API base URL
- Build command

No debug signing may be represented as production signing.

No Play Store submission is required.

The target is a production-ready direct-install APK.

==================================================
5. COMMIT AND PUSH THE FIX
==================================================

Commit the Android CI fix to:

Repository:
ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform

Branch:
main

Return:

- Files changed
- Commit message
- Commit SHA
- Push status
- GitHub main HEAD SHA

Do not stop after the local fix.

==================================================
6. RUN GITHUB ACTIONS TO GREEN
==================================================

Trigger or allow the real GitHub Actions workflow to run on the new commit.

Required results:

- Backend tests: PASS
- Android release consistency: PASS
- Security checks: PASS
- Independence audit: PASS
- Build validation: PASS
- APK job: PASS if configured for this trigger, or clearly SKIPPED only by documented workflow condition

Return:

- Workflow run ID
- Workflow URL reference
- Commit SHA
- Every job status
- Start time
- Completion time
- Final workflow status

PASS requires the full required workflow to be green.

==================================================
7. VERIFY RENDER DEPLOYMENT AFTER GREEN CI
==================================================

Verify the current commit is deployed to:

API:
ivx-holdings-platform

Worker:
ivx-senior-dev-01

Return:

- API service ID
- API deployment ID
- API live SHA
- Worker service ID
- Worker deployment ID
- Worker live SHA
- GitHub HEAD SHA
- Auto-deploy status
- Deployment timestamps

All live SHAs must match the approved GitHub SHA.

==================================================
8. LIVE PRODUCTION CHECKS
==================================================

Run:

- https://ivxholding.com/
- https://ivxholding.com/robots.txt
- https://ivxholding.com/sitemap.xml
- https://api.ivxholding.com/health
- https://api.ivxholding.com/version
- Public chat
- Worker status without authorization

Expected:

- Website HTTP 200
- robots.txt HTTP 200
- sitemap.xml HTTP 200
- /health HTTP 200
- /version HTTP 200
- /version SHA matches GitHub HEAD
- Public chat HTTP 200
- Protected worker status without authorization returns 401
- No secrets returned

==================================================
9. EXECUTE THE INDEPENDENCE CUTOVER
==================================================

Only after CI is green and production is healthy:

Run the prepared independence cutover from an IVX-controlled checkout.

Use the existing cutover tooling only after reviewing it.

Required result:

- Remove rork.json
- Remove references that require rork.json
- Preserve useful IVX-owned independence audit scripts
- Remove obsolete Rork sandbox registration
- Rewrite any remaining build scripts to standard IVX scripts
- Confirm Metro, Expo, backend, and worker do not require Rork config

Do not run destructive deletion without verifying the script contents first.

==================================================
10. REMOVE ORPHANED RORK ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
==================================================

After confirming zero active readers, remove:

- EXPO_PUBLIC_RORK_API_BASE_URL
- EXPO_PUBLIC_RORK_APP_KEY
- EXPO_PUBLIC_RORK_AUTH_URL
- EXPO_PUBLIC_RORK_FUNCTIONS_URL
- EXPO_PUBLIC_RORK_TOOLKIT_SECRET_KEY
- EXPO_PUBLIC_TOOLKIT_URL

Return for each:

- Environment/service
- Before: PRESENT / MISSING
- Active reader count
- Removal status
- Restart required
- Verification result

Never display secret values.

If Rork cannot remove them from the dashboard, return exact manual owner steps.

==================================================
11. ROTATE LEGACY TOOLKIT CREDENTIALS
==================================================

If any old Rork toolkit credential ever existed:

- Identify the provider/account
- Revoke or rotate it
- Verify production does not use it
- Confirm no source or environment reference remains

Do not rotate current IVX production credentials unnecessarily.

==================================================
12. RE-RUN THE COMPLETE RORK DEPENDENCY AUDIT
==================================================

Search the entire repository and runtime for:

- rork
- rork.com
- r2-pub.rork.com
- @rork-ai/toolkit-sdk
- rork.json
- EXPO_PUBLIC_RORK_
- RORK_API_KEY
- RORK_TOKEN
- RORK_SECRET
- Rork proxy URLs
- Rork webhooks
- Rork telemetry
- Rork build hooks

Classify all remaining matches:

- Active production dependency
- Active development dependency
- Historical documentation
- Defensive blocklist
- Audit tooling
